the422Diagnosis.mechanismChosen: B -- a serve-guard refusal, never reaching a body with recordRetirement, so rule 2 cannot and does not clear this parcel.
the422Diagnosis.mechanismRejected: A -- the retirement is served but the walk grades it wrong. Ruled out because gradeParcelResponse's control flow (unchanged by this diff) returns BP-MEANING-01 on any non-ok HTTP response BEFORE the retirement-aware branch is ever reached; a 422 never produces a JSON body the retirement check could act on in the first place.
evidence: Live probe, 2026-09-09: `curl -sS -w '\nHTTP_STATUS:%{http_code}\n' https://smart-site-factory.vercel.app/site/api/spine/cortex/api/brokerage/v1/place/node/48055:1/facets` returned `{"error":"SITUS_PUNCTUATION_ONLY","errorClass":"serve_refused","message":"situs is punctuation only"}` / `HTTP_STATUS:422`.

Code read (LDT pinned SHA 3885efad, artifacts/api-server/src/routes/brokerageNodeFacets.ts): the node/:parcelNodeId/facets handler's Promise.all is wrapped in try/catch; on err.code === 'ACCESS_NOT_DEFAULTED' || 'SITUS_PUNCTUATION_ONLY' it responds 422 and returns BEFORE `snapshot` (and therefore any recordRetirement-bearing body) is produced. The throw originates in lib/serveGuards.ts's refusePayloadAtServe -> assertSitusNotPunctuationOnly, called from loadBakedNodeFacetSnapshot.

Correction to the dispatch's own prior assumption: it named ACCESS_NOT_DEFAULTED as the historical 422 cause for this program. The live cause for 48055:1 specifically is SITUS_PUNCTUATION_ONLY -- a different code, but the same mechanism SHAPE (a pre-body serve-guard throw). Recording this because DEV_PROCESS 3.2a requires a correction to carry the same evidentiary standard as the claim it corrects: this is quoted from the live response, not inferred from the dispatch's guess.

LESSON: A predicate this dispatch says to IMPORT rather than reimplement can be imported at runtime by adding a new esbuild entry (bundling the library file itself, not a CLI wrapper) to an EXISTING bake-CLI-bundle build script, then dynamically importing the bundle. Two non-obvious runtime hazards this exposed and their fixes: (1) a transitively-bundled shared DB-client module can throw at MODULE-EVAL time if its expected env var (here, DATABASE_URL, distinct from this program's own FACTORY_DATABASE_URL) is absent -- fixable with a placeholder set only for the duration of the one import, since a `pg` Pool's construction is lazy and never actually connects; (2) esbuild's generated CJS-interop shim for a lazily-`require`d Node builtin deep in the bundle graph can throw 'Dynamic require of X is not supported' specifically under node's OWN test-runner module loader while working fine under plain `node` -- fixed by the SAME `globalThis.require = createRequire(import.meta.url)` banner an existing sibling bundle script already carries for its own entries; a new entry added to a build script with multiple existing entries needs to inherit ALL of that script's existing accommodations, not just its entry-point list.

Diagnosing a specific parcel's HTTP 422 by reading serve-side code alone can name the right MECHANISM SHAPE (a pre-body serve-guard throw) while getting the specific CODE wrong (SITUS_PUNCTUATION_ONLY, not the historically-assumed ACCESS_NOT_DEFAULTED) -- a live curl against the real staging endpoint settled it in one request and is cheap enough to always do before trusting a historical assumption, even one repeated in a dispatch's own text.

DEAD_END: Assuming NODE_PATH would make an in-process ESM `import()` of a bundle placed outside the consuming project's own directory tree resolve that project's `pg` dependency -- NODE_PATH is documented as CJS-require-only and is not consulted by the ESM loader at all; the bundle must live somewhere under the consuming project's own root so ordinary ancestor-directory node_modules resolution finds it (which is also, independently, exactly why /app/bakes/*.mjs resolves 'pg' against /app/node_modules/pg in the real Cloud image -- not because of the Dockerfile's NODE_PATH env var, which only matters for CJS).
